  2. Centre extends ban on fugitive preacher Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation for another five years; Home Minister Amit Shah says, the outfit propagates terrorism and separatism.

  3. India records all-time high exports of nearly 90 billion US Dollars in October this year, showing strong resilience and growth.

<><><> 

         

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, India is moving towards global leadership in emerging technologies, from chips to ships, and from Artificial Intelligence and data centres to quantum computing. He emphasized that reliable power generation is essential to achieving this ambition. Mr Modi said the country is expanding its nuclear power capacity as part of its efforts to achieve clean energy goals and meet its growing energy requirements. The Prime Minister was addressing the gathering  at Bengaluru in Karnataka yesterday, after launching development projects worth over 15,600 crore rupees. Mr Modi said the projects, covering metro, railways and energy infrastructure, will strengthen connectivity, boost economic growth and create new employment opportunities in the state. 

 

 

 

The Prime Minister also inaugurated the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium yesterday evening. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Modi highlighted India’s growing achievements in space science, astronomy and research, saying that the country’s expanding capabilities in these fields are creating new opportunities for young people and contributing to improving life on Earth.  He said the facility will add a new chapter to Mysuru’s contribution to India’s scientific journey and help nurture scientific curiosity among students.

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

 

Prime Minister reached Ahmedabad in Gujarat from Karnataka’s Mysuru last evening. He was received at the airport by Gujarat Governor Acharya Devvrat and Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. The Prime Minister subsequently reached Gandhinagar, where he stayed overnight at Lok Bhavan.
         

 

The Prime Minister’s scheduled visit to the Ambaji Temple in Banaskantha district today has been postponed in view of the large number of devotees visiting the shrine during the festive season.
         

 

Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said, the decision to reschedule the visit was taken to ensure that devotees do not face inconvenience due to security arrangements for the Prime Minister.

The Centre has extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) led by fugitive preacher Dr Zakir Naik for another five years. The Ministry of Home Affairs, declared IRF an unlawful association under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, citing the organisation’s involvement in activities detrimental to the country’s security, communal harmony and secular fabric.
         

 

In a social media post, the Office of Union Home Minister Amit Shah said, the decision reflected the government’s commitment to its policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism and anti-national activities. The post said, the organisation had been involved in activities aimed at inciting communal hatred, promoting terrorism and spreading separatist ideology. More from our correspondent

 

         

 

According to the Home Ministry notification, the government had first declared the Islamic Research Foundation an unlawful association in November, 2016. The ban was subsequently extended in November, 2021. The Ministry said, the IRF had been indulging in activities prejudicial to the security of the country, with the potential to disturb peace and communal harmony and disrupt the secular fabric of the country. The Ministry also cited speeches and statements made by the foundation’s founder and president, Dr Zakir Naik, saying they promoted enmity and hatred among different religious communities and inspired young people belonging to a particular religion, both in India and abroad, to commit terrorist acts. SHIVANG MISRA, AKASHAVNI NEWS, DELHI.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tributes to former Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary today. Pandit Nehru was born on this day in the year 1889 at Anand Bhawan in Prayagraj.

 Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said, India recorded an all-time high in exports, reaching nearly 90 billion dollars in October this year. Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the India International Trade Fair (IITF) in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said export figure of October comprised around 50 billion dollars in merchandise exports and 40 billion dollars in services exports. He further informed that India’s cumulative exports during the first seven months of the current financial year, up to October, has reached 570 billion dollars. Expressing confidence in the country’s export performance, the Minister said India is well on course to achieve its one-trillion-dollar export target this year.

 

 

 

 

 

The annual India International Trade Fair, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, begins in New Delhi today. It brings together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad. The theme of this year’s fair is ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. A total of 32 States and Union Territories will participate in the 14-day event, showcasing their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, cultural heritage, tourism potential and development initiatives.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The festival of Chhath is being observed with religious fervour and devotion across the country, particularly in Bihar, Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Delhi.

 

 

 On the second day of the four-day festival, devotees will be observing the traditional Kharna ritual today.
         

 

On the occasion, devotees observe a day-long fast, abstaining from both food and water. More from our correspondent:

 

         

 

“Kharna, which signifies purity and sanctity, is an important ritual of the Chhath festival. On this day, devotees observe a day-long fast and perform special prayers in the evening. They then partake of the traditional prasad, which includes jaggery-based kheer, roti and bananas.

 

With this ritual begins the rigorous 36-hour fast, during which devotees abstain from both food and water.

 

Meanwhile, the festive spirit of Chhath is visible across the state, including the capital city of Patna. Traditional Chhath songs have filled the air with devotional fervour. Markets are witnessing brisk sales of bamboo baskets, soop, fruits and earthen stoves, which are essential for the rituals.Savita Pareek, Akashvani News, Patna.”

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has temporarily halted departing flights across the country following a telecommunications failure that affected air traffic control centres, disrupting thousands of flights across the country. According to flight-tracking services, nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled following the ground stop. The FAA said the communications outage affected all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centres across the United States, prompting the suspension of departures as a precautionary measure.
         

 

Later, the US authorities lifted the nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights and stranded passengers across the country, clearing the way for airlines to resume operations after more than four hours.
         

 

Meanwhile, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, FAA technicians are investigating the communications failure. Aircraft already in the air were allowed to land, while departing flights were temporarily suspended.

Air India has issued a travel advisory warning of possible consequential disruptions to its flights to and from the United States. The advisory has been issued following a nationwide ground stop across US airports due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations. The airline has advised passengers to check the latest flight status on its official website and plan their journey to the airport accordingly. Air India said, their teams are closely monitoring the situation and will share the further updates.

The Ministry of External Affairs has reiterated that the safety and well-being of Indian seafarers abroad remain a top priority for the government. Briefing media in New Delhi, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said an emergency travel certificate has been issued to Indian seafarer Akshay Harish from Keralam who was stranded at Chabahar Port in Iran, paving the way for his early return to India.

In Men’s Cricket, India will take on arch-rivals Pakistan in the final of the Under-19 Asia Cup at Muscat in Oman, today. The summit clash is scheduled to begin at 10:30 AM Indian Standard Time.
         

 

The Indian team will be looking to avenge its group-stage defeat against Pakistan and reclaim the continental title after missing out on the trophy in the previous three editions. India will be aiming to clinch a record-extending ninth Under-19 Asia Cup title, while defending champions Pakistan will be looking to lift the trophy for the third time.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands today. The Met Department said that thunderstorm accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Rajasthan.

India has achieved a significant milestone in its fight against tuberculosis (TB), recording a 38 percent reduction in TB mortality since 2015. This is higher than the global reduction of 35 per cent, reflecting the country’s sustained efforts towards eliminating the disease.

 

India’s reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality highlights the country’s strong performance in reducing TB-related deaths. According to the World Health Organization’s Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, released yesterday, India has also achieved an impressive 94 per cent treatment success rate among patients suffering from tuberculosis. Health and Family Welfare Ministry said that the progress reflects the impact of intensified interventions under the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including proactive case finding including use of AI enabled X-rays, rapid diagnostics, prompt treatment initiation, differentiated TB care and nutritional support. WITH SHIVANG, NITIKA GUPTA AKASHVANI NEWS DELHI.

President Droupadi Murmu will confer the National Sports Awards 2025 at a ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning. India’s premier women’s badminton doubles pair, Treesa Jolly and Pullela Gayatri Gopichand, along with fifteen other sportspersons from various disciplines, will be conferred the Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in Sports and Games. Veteran Indian footballer Isaiah Arumainayagam will receive the Arjuna Award (Lifetime). Athletics coach Parveer Singh, boxing coach Chhote Lal Yadav and shooting coach Neha Nandkumar Chavan will be honoured with the Dronacharya Award.

 

Meanwhile, the Army Paralympic Node, Pune, will receive the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two day visit to Karnataka and Gujarat beginning today. Mr Modi will inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off various development projects worth over 15 thousand 600 crore rupees in Bengaluru this morning. These projects span key sectors including urban mobility, power transmission, renewable energy, petroleum infrastructure, waste management and railways.The Prime Minister will inaugurate the much awaited Metro Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to S G Palya station and flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express, providing faster and modern rail connectivity between Bengaluru, Coastal Karnataka and Goa.

 

After arriving today morning, the Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, the campus of Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana. Thereafter the Prime Minister will travel in the new Metro Pink line and launch various development projects at IIM Bengaluru. These include, inauguration of and foundation stone laying for various power transmission schemes in the state. He will dedicate India’s largest underground LPG storage cavern in Mangaluru, dedicate to the nation the Devangonthi marketing terminal of MRPL refinery and lay the foundation stone for GAIL Compressed Biogas Plant.  Mr Modi will also inaugurate four redeveloped railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme at Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subramanya Road. PONNUMON AKASHVANI NEWS BENGALURU.

The Prime Minister will also flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express today. Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will be present on the occasion.

 

Talking to reporters in Mangaluru last night, Mr Vaishnaw said that the important service will connect coastal Karnataka with Bengaluru.

 

“The 16-coach Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express will comprise Executive Chair coaches and Chair Car coaches, offering passengers a modern and comfortable travel experience. The service will benefit passengers across Bengaluru Urban, Hassan, Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and Uttara Kannada districts, as well as South Goa. Its key features include bio-vacuum toilets with touch-free amenities, automatic doors, onboard infotainment systems, and revolving seats in Executive Class. The train will also have specially designed lavatories for Divyangjan passengers and can reach 100 kilometres per hour in just 52 seconds. The new Vande Bharat is also equipped with Kavach safety system, which is an indigenous Train Collision Avoidance System. RISHU JAISWAL, AKASHVANI NEWS, MANGALURU.”

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has proposed reforms to simplify the rules for governing cab rental businesses, promote ease of doing business and strengthen passenger safety. Under the proposed reforms, operators will be allowed to offer cabs with or without drivers. The minimum fleet requirement will be reduced from 50 to five vehicles, with at least 2 cabs per place of operation. The requirement for branches in five tourist cities is removed. The reforms also include a single electronic licence, valid across the State or Union Territory for a uniform fee. Approved places of operation may include airports, stations and bus terminals. It further added that licence grants and renewals have a proposed 60-day timeline. Adding or removing cabs or places of operation has a 30 day deemed-approval mechanism.

The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will be inaugurated at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue.

 

The IITF 2026 is being organised under the theme ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. The fair will host business days from the 14th to 18th of this month, offering opportunities for trade visitors and business-to-business networking. From 19th to 27th November, the fair will open its doors to the general public, families and cultural visitors.

The four-day long Chhath Puja will begin today with the ‘Nahay-Khay’ ritual in different parts of the country. Dedicated to Surya Dev or the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, the festival is observed with strict purity, fasting, and rituals along riverbanks and ghats. The Nahay-Khay’ is marked by ritual bathing and preparation of food while observing strict cleanliness and purity. Traditionally, devotees prepare Kaddubhaat as prasad, marking the beginning of the four-day festival.

 

The second day will be observed as ‘Kharna’. Devotees will observe a day-long fast and break it in the evening after offering prayers and consuming prasad. This will be followed by the rigorous ‘nirjala’ fast.
On the third day, devotees will gather at rivers, ponds and other Chhath ghats in the evening to worship Chhathi Maiya and offer ‘arghya’ to the setting sun.

The festival will conclude on Monday morning with devotees offering ‘arghya’ to the rising sun.

<><><> 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today extended his greetings to fellow citizens on the commencement of the four-day Chhath Mahaparv, a festival of popular faith and worship of the Sun God. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that today marks Nahay-Khay, the first day of the festival. He extended his greetings to all devotees observing the fast and wished that everyone receives the blessings of Chhathi Maiya.

The countdown to the 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, begins in Goa today, with the curtain raiser press conference scheduled this morning. The nine-day festival will be held from November 20 to 28 in Goa. Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant will grace the curtain raiser programme.

 

The curtain raiser press conference will be held at 9:30 AM at Dona Paula in Goa. Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar, and IFFI Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker will also attend the programme. The press conference is expected to unveil the festival’s major attractions, special programmes and key highlights, setting the stage for the 57th edition of IFFI. NIKHIL UPADHYAY, AKASHVANI NEWS, PANAJI.

The SPARSH Outreach Programme, aimed at resolving all grievances of defence pensioners under a single roof, will be held today in Thiruvananthapuram. The programme is being organised by the Controller of Defence Accounts, Chennai.

 

“The initiative aims to ensure immediate resolution of pension related complaints, irrespective of how long they have been pending. Officials from banks and record offices will be present with all the necessary official documents to settle grievances on the spot.

 

The arrangement is expected to spare defence pensioners the inconvenience of visiting multiple offices and banks to resolve their complaints.

 

 Defence Ministry sources informed that the facilities for issuing pension payment orders, annual identification of pensioners and updating their profiles will also be available at the venue. SMITHY M PALLURUTHY, AKASHVANI NEWS, THIRUVANANTHAPURAM.”

Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to let European representatives join the next round of Ukraine peace talks. US envoy Steve Witkoff informed this to reporters after the talks. Witkoff told Russian state TV after meeting Putin in the Kremlin that the move to give Europe a seat at the negotiating table at the next round of talks is a breakthrough.

 

But Putin’s comments that Washington must work with its European allies to understand if they ‌want peace or war in Ukraine, underlined how difficult the negotiations could become, given sharp differences between Moscow and European capitals. Kyiv and Moscow ⁠said after two days of ⁠trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi this week that  there had been some progress but that major differences remained, including on territorial issues.

India, led by Shreyas Iyer, will look to continue their winning momentum after taking an unassailable 2-nil lead in the five-match series. The third ODI in Hamilton was abandoned due to rain. New Zealand will aim to bounce back and register their first win in the series.

Union Cabinet has approved the development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in the North and South Block complex in New Delhi. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation.

The Cabinet has also approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for RABI Season, 2026-27 on Phosphatic and Potassic fertilizers. The tentative budgetary requirement for Rabi 2026-27 will be approximately 62 thousand 370 crore rupees. This is nearly 24 thousand 417 crore more than the budgetary requirement for Rabi 2025-26 season. Mr Vaishnaw said the subsidy will ensure smooth availability of these fertilizers to the farmers at affordable prices.

The Cabinet has also given nod to the continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031.

The Cabinet has also cleared the extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04 of Noida Metro Rail Project covering approximately 8.5 kilometres and comprising five elevated stations.

<><><> 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stated that the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum will transform New Delhi into a global centre of cultural heritage, with the world’s largest museum display area. In a social media post, the Prime Minister noted that the Cabinet’s decision will give impetus to the transformation of the historic North and South Block buildings into a magnificent celebration of India’s civilisational journey.

Mr Modi said the museum will showcase thousands of years of India’s heritage through world-class galleries and immersive experiences. It will cover a wide range of subjects, including ancient knowledge systems, mathematics, astronomy, architecture, art, languages, and spirituality. He highlighted that these buildings, which have long served as centres of governance, will now become places where millions can discover, experience, and celebrate the timeless richness of India’s civilisation.

The Prime Minister described the initiative as a historic new chapter in India’s cultural heritage.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi this evening. Around 2,000 farmers from across India, alongside policymakers, diplomats, industry leaders, and agricultural scientists are attending the 2-day event. Approximately 20 progressive farmers and Padma Shri recipients are scheduled to share their innovation and resilience stories. Discussions center on increasing farmer incomes, adopting precision farming and artificial intelligence-led resource management, developing climate-resilient crops, and expanding India’s agricultural exports.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two day visit to Karnataka and Gujarat beginning tomorrow.

Mr Modi will participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram,  the residential headquarters campus of Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana (S-VYASA) tomorrow morning. In the afternoon, the Prime Minister will flag off and undertake a metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station. After this, Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 15 thousand 600 crore rupees in Bengaluru.

On the same day, the Prime Minister will travel to Mysuru where, he will participate in a tree plantation programme at Bharat Vann. In the evening, he will inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium.

Government has rationalized the visa regime by reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to 9 and the number of sub-categories from 49 to 23. Ministry of Home Affairs said that the move is aimed at boosting foreign tourist arrivals, enhance medical value travel and foreign student arrivals. The step follows the earlier rationalisation undertaken in October last year when the main visa categories were reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49. Ministry said that the required filed and column for all 23 categories and sub-categories of Visas have been reduced by 65 to 70 per cent.

Today is the Public Service Broadcasting Day. The day is observed every year on this day to mark the historic address of Father of the nation Mahatma Gandhi, through Akashvani. An important day in the History of Broadcasting, Mahatma Gandhi paid his first and only visit to the Broadcasting House in New Delhi on this day in 1947. More from our correspondent:

“On this day in 1947, Mahatma Gandhi addressed the grief-stricken people staying in Kurukshetra who were displaced during partition through a special broadcast. In the year 2000, then Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting, Sushma Swaraj announced that every 12th of November would henceforth be observed as Public Service Broadcasting Day. Since then, Akashvani has been celebrating the occasion every year with special programmes and events. Akashvani music artists render bhajans dear to Mahatma Gandhi to mark these celebrations. Throughout the year, Akashvani broadcasts and organizes a series of special programmes across the country based on the Gandhian Philosophy. Public Service Broadcasting Day inspires Broadcasters to carry forward the ideals and teachings of Mahatma Gandhi, to every corner of the country. With Arzoo, Samarth Singh for Akashvani News, Delhi.”

The Northern Railway is operating 29 Special trains from major railway stations in the Delhi region today. The move is aimed at facilitating passengers travelling to their native places to celebrate the Chhath festival. The move is part of the elaborate arrangements made by Northern Railway at major stations of Delhi Area for the convenience of passengers, especially those travelling to the Eastern parts of the country to celebrate the festival of Chhath.

Ministry of Tribal Affairs will organise a two-day National Tribal Literary Festival beginning today at India Habitat Centre in New Delhi. The Literary Festival is being held as part of the celebrations commemorating Janjatiya Gaurav Divas 2026. The festival aims to provide a national platform for celebrating India’s rich and diverse tribal literary traditions, promoting indigenous languages and oral narratives, and recognising the contributions of tribal writers, poets, storytellers and knowledge holders. The inaugural session will be attended by Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram.

Iran has refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or resume negotiations with the United States until Washington meets seven conditions set by Tehran. We have a report:

“Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said that Tehran has sent its demands to Washington but is awaiting an official response. He warned President Donald Trump against renewed military action, saying it will result in another US defeat. Senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei also said no negotiations are underway and warned that Iran can target US military bases outside the Middle East if they were used to launch attacks against the country. Iran’s demands include lifting US sanctions, releasing frozen assets, ending the naval blockade of Iranian ports, compensation for war damage and an end to fighting across regional fronts, including Lebanon. Tehran’s proposal calls for reopening the Strait of Hormuz six days after Washington meets its demands, with negotiations on a final agreement beginning the following day. Jigyasa Pandey, Akashvani News Delhi.”

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange colour warning for heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms over Jammu and Kashmir today. Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days. Similar weather conditions are expected over Keralam, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for the day. IMD has advised fishermen to avoid venturing into the Andaman Sea till the 16th of this month.

An earthquake measuring 4.9 on the Richter scale shook Darjeeling and adjoining areas of North Bengal in the early hours today. The tremors were recorded at around 4:30 AM. According to the National Centre for Seismology, the earthquake had its epicentre in Nepal. Tremors were felt across several parts of North Bengal and neighbouring regions. Residents, particularly those living in high-rise buildings, were startled by the sudden shaking, with many rushing outdoors as a precaution.

Indian boxers, Gunjan and Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei have stormed into the finals of the Summer Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, keeping India’s hopes of two gold medals alive. India and the European Union have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with Horizon Europe, the bloc’s 93.5-billion-euro flagship research and innovation funding programme. Under the arrangement, Indian researchers, businesses and research organisations will be eligible to receive direct funding from Horizon Europe and lead international collaborative research projects under its second pillar, which focuses on global challenges and European industrial competitiveness. Once signed and ratified by both sides, the agreement is expected to come into effect in January next year.

 

“The Horizon Europe programme covers key areas such as healthcare, artificial intelligence, digital technology, space, climate, energy and industrial development. The European Commission said the agreement marks a significant milestone in India-EU relations and will strengthen scientific cooperation, create new research opportunities and deepen their strategic partnership. Horizon Europe currently includes 23 associated non-EU countries, ranging from the United Kingdom, Canada, and Japan to South Korea and Switzerland. The association will enable Indian institutions to receive grants directly from the European Commission and allow Indian scientists to lead and coordinate major international research projects, on terms similar to those available to organisations in EU member states, in the covered areas. The agreement is expected to give a fresh impetus to India-EU scientific and technological cooperation and strengthen collaboration in emerging technologies and innovation. Rishu Jaiswal, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

The National Health Authority, under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reviewed the progress of two flagship healthcare initiatives, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).
